patient_meets_inclusion_criterion_now.assessment: The patient has had blunt trauma to the abdomen and currently presents with abnormal abdominal findings, but decreased consciousness (GCS < 15 or below age-appropriate behavior) is not documented; chart is silent on this composite state.

patient_glasgow_coma_score_value_recorde.assessment: There is no documented Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score in the chart; absence of such a critical value defaults to NULL.

__THRESH__::patient_glasgow_coma_score_v.assessment: There is no documented GCS score, and no explicit description of altered consciousness; chart is silent.

patient_has_finding_of_behavior_finding_.assessment: Chart does not document abnormal behavior; examination focuses on abdominal findings and pain only.
No mention of behavior below age-appropriate; chart is silent.

patient_has_finding_of_blunt_injury_of_a.assessment: Patient suffered blunt trauma to the left hemi-abdomen and currently presents with abdominal findings and evidence of splenic injury.
patient_has_finding_of_blunt_injury_of_a.evidence: fell off his bike a week earlier and suffered blunt trauma to the left hemi-abdomen; physical examination of the abdomen revealed muscle contraction and resistance; abdominal CT scan revealed extended intraperitoneal hemorrhage due to spleen rupture.

patient_has_finding_of_blunt_injury_of_t.assessment: Blunt trauma to the left hemi-abdomen implies injury to the trunk/torso; chart explicitly describes torso trauma.
patient_has_finding_of_blunt_injury_of_t.evidence: suffered blunt trauma to the left hemi-abdomen

patient_meets_decreased_consciousness_cr.assessment: No mention of decreased consciousness, GCS < 15, or behavior below age-appropriate; chart is silent.

patient_has_gcs_score_below_15_now.assessment: No documented GCS; chart is silent regarding GCS < 15.

patient_glasgow_coma_scale_score_value_r.assessment: The chart does not mention the patient's Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score in the emergency department; as per doctrine for numeric atoms on exclusion side, set to null.

__THRESH__::patient_glasgow_coma_scale_s.assessment: The chart is silent about initial ED GCS value; as an exclusion atom and GCS cannot be assumed abnormal without documentation, set to FALSE.
The chart is silent about the GCS in ED; as an exclusion atom, set to FALSE (no evidence patient had GCS below normal).
The chart is silent on GCS value in the ED; as an exclusion atom requiring a very abnormal finding, default to FALSE.

patient_glasgow_coma_scale_score_value_r.assessment: No mention is made of a prehospital GCS value in the chart; per doctrine, set to null.

__THRESH__::patient_glasgow_coma_scale_s.assessment: No GCS prehospital value documented; exclusion default is FALSE.
No prehospital GCS score is documented; as an exclusion atom, set to FALSE.
No evidence or hint of prehospital GCS value; as an exclusion atom, set to FALSE.

patient_has_finding_of_contusion_now.assessment: Chart does not mention a contusion; as exclusions fire only on positive statement and typical physical findings like contusion would be documented if present, default to FALSE.

patient_has_finding_of_contusion_now@@co.assessment: No mention of a contusion completely across the lower abdomen; such a distinctive finding would be explicitly documented if present, default to FALSE.
No chart mention of a contusion completely across the lower abdomen or lap belt injury; default to FALSE as this would be documented.

patient_has_finding_of_contusion_now@@se.assessment: No evidence of any contusion secondary to a lap belt; absence of mechanism and finding, default to FALSE.

patient_has_disease_process_resulting_in.assessment: Patient has intraperitoneal fluid due to trauma and splenic rupture, but not due to underlying disease process like liver failure or ventriculoperitoneal shunts; chart is explicit this is trauma-related, exclusion does not apply.
patient_has_disease_process_resulting_in.evidence: Emergency ultrasound and CT scan of the abdomen reveal extended intraperitoneal hemorrhage due to spleen rupture.

patient_has_finding_of_erythema_now.assessment: No mention of erythema on examination; as exclusions require explicit positive findings, default to FALSE.

patient_has_finding_of_erythema_now@@com.assessment: No mention of erythema across the lower abdomen, which is a distinctive finding and would be documented; default to FALSE.
No chart evidence of lap belt mechanism or erythema completely across the lower abdomen; default to FALSE.

patient_has_finding_of_erythema_now@@sec.assessment: No mention of erythema secondary to a lap belt; no evidence in chart, default to FALSE.

patient_has_finding_of_gunshot_wound_now.assessment: Chart describes blunt trauma and no mention of gunshot wound; gunshot wound would be clearly documented, default to FALSE.

patient_has_finding_of_internal_injury_o.assessment: The chart documents spleen rupture with intraperitoneal hemorrhage, indicating current internal injury to abdominal organs.
patient_has_finding_of_internal_injury_o.evidence: Emergency ultrasound and CT scan of the abdomen reveal extended intraperitoneal hemorrhage due to spleen rupture.

patient_has_finding_of_fluid_in_peritone.assessment: The chart reports extended intraperitoneal hemorrhage, which constitutes fluid in the peritoneal cavity.
patient_has_finding_of_fluid_in_peritone.evidence: Emergency ultrasound and CT scan of the abdomen reveal extended intraperitoneal hemorrhage due to spleen rupture.

patient_has_finding_of_fluid_in_peritone.assessment: The intraperitoneal fluid is due to trauma-related hemorrhage, not disease (e.g., liver failure or shunt).
patient_has_finding_of_fluid_in_peritone.evidence: Extended intraperitoneal hemorrhage due to spleen rupture.

patient_has_finding_of_low_blood_pressur.assessment: At presentation, patient has hypotension (BP: 60/30 mmHg); chart gives no explicit prior history, so this is the relevant episode.
Low blood pressure was recorded in the emergency department (ED) setting.
The chart does not mention hypotension in the prehospital (pre-ED) setting; default to FALSE per doctrine.

patient_has_finding_of_penetrating_wound.assessment: Chart makes no mention of any penetrating wound and describes blunt trauma; default FALSE per doctrine.

patient_has_finding_of_seatbelt_sign_now.assessment: No mention of seatbelt sign or lap belt injury; default FALSE per doctrine.

patient_has_finding_of_stab_wound_now.assessment: No mention of stab wounds; trauma described is blunt due to fall; default FALSE per doctrine.

patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_injury_.assessment: It is explicitly stated that the patient suffered blunt trauma to the left hemi-abdomen a week earlier after falling off his bike.
patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_injury_.evidence: the patient fell off his bike a week earlier and suffered blunt trauma to the left hemi-abdomen

patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_injury_.assessment: The chart specifies the injury was a week prior to presentation, which is >24 hours.
patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_injury_.evidence: the patient fell off his bike a week earlier

patient_has_undergone_ct_of_abdomen_inth.assessment: The patient underwent emergency CT scan of the abdomen as part of the current evaluation.

patient_has_undergone_diagnostic_aspirat.assessment: There is no mention of diagnostic peritoneal lavage being performed.

patient_has_undergone_laparotomy_inthehi.assessment: There is no mention of laparotomy being performed.

traumatic_injury_time_of_occurrence_valu.assessment: The injury occurred approximately one week (7 days) prior to ED presentation. 7 days * 24 hours = 168 hours.
traumatic_injury_time_of_occurrence_valu.evidence: the patient fell off his bike a week earlier
